facts.statement: Longosuchus is an extinct genus of desmatosuchin aetosaur that lived during the Late Triassic in North America.
facts.quote: Longosuchus (meaning "Long's crocodile") is an extinct genus of desmatosuchin aetosaur from the Late Triassic of North America.

facts.statement: Longosuchus measured approximately 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Longosuchus measured about 3 metres in length.

facts.statement: Fossils reported from Morocco are likely misidentified scutes belonging to a paratypothoracin aetosaur rather than Longosuchus.
facts.quote: Reported fossils from Morocco are likely misidentified scutes of a paratypothoracin aetosaur.

facts.statement: The species was originally named T. meadei in 1947 based on skeletal remains found in the Otis Chalk quarries in Howard County, western Texas.
facts.quote: Longosuchus was originally named as a species of Typothorax, T. meadei, in 1947 on the basis of skeletal remains from the Otis Chalk quarries in Howard County, western Texas.

facts.statement: Hunt and Lucas renamed the species Longosuchus in 1990 after recognizing it as distinct from Typothorax and honoring Robert Long.
facts.quote: Hunt and Lucas (1990) recognized T. meadei as generically distinct from the type species of Typothorax and renamed it Longosuchus in honor of Robert Long.

facts.statement: Longosuchus is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Longosuchus belongs to the subfamily Desmatosuchinae.
Longosuchus lived between 237 and 205.7 million years ago, spanning the Carnian to Norian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Longosuchus is the tribe Desmatosuchini.
